listing.name: Auto Colonies
listing.summary: Automatic Faction and Colony management for Starsector 0.98a+0.98.5a.
listing.aiSummary: Automatically manages colonies, including building upgrades, resource distribution, military defense, and economic balancing.

description:
My mods are fully AI created mods that I created for my own playthroughs and have posted since I use them every time I play, and figured someone else may also find some use for them. If you use them and find any issues, stemming from either AI development wonkiness or just oversight on my part, let me know in the comments here or on github, either is fine, and I'll try to get things fixed quickly. The biggest advantage to slop is speed.

Auto Colonies
Automatic Faction and Colony management for Starsector 0.98a+0.98.5a.

Source code and guides
Required mods: None.
Updating: Delete the old folder in mods/ and extract the new one, or just use TriOS. Saves and settings carry over.
Safe to add mid-game

Safe to remove after Prepare for removal

No known mod conflicts

Story mode (default)
The mod starts on a new save with a PDA message. Choose which one you want!
Playing through the story takes you past the normal autopilot to some truly game-breaking end-tier colony stuff.
New games use Story by default, and it's what I recommend. Story will be balanced depending on how many mods you have installed that add AI cores to the drop pool. The more you have, the more expensive the mod will be to use as far as AI core bandwidth

This is the intended way to play!

Normal mode
The more boring option but it just does its job as advertised on the tin. Automatically manages your colonies, does a decent job at it, protects them, automatically upgrades, replaces buildings, etc. Has most of the features of the story mode but not a lot of the "cool" stuff.
Pick the other option that isn't story if you'd rather just have access to it immediately, like if you added it mid-save and you don't want to bother with any of the story stuff.

Even though this is the more basic version, either way it's still not going to be free. This is still going to cost credits to run. Every decision it makes will come with a small cost. This is configurable in settings.

How to access the mod

Main tab

Settings tab

You can switch any time in LunaLib (F3), under Auto Colonies, and each save keeps its story progress.

Features
Building
There are several profiles to pick from. The default is balanced and it will try to use all the mods you have installed to optimize what buildings to build.
Items, AI cores and administrators
For a small fee, depending on what settings you choose, these will go in the slots that your doctrine says. Basically you insert them into the Autopilot storage in your colonies and Autopilot, for a fee, will ship them around to the colonies that need them and insert them automatically. AI cores have a special ruling that's different than items and administrators, which you should definitely set depending on what you want to do.
Money ladder and capital
It puts money where it matters most, in this order:
It stockpiles first, then grows colonies.
Then it builds up the military, with new ships and more patrols.
Then it makes new colonies.
Then it balances your whole economy.
Last, it builds wonders, optimizes everything and picks your biggest colony as the capital (you can change that in the settings).

War
It handles war decently well. Depending on what you pick it will either just do nothing all the way up to scorched earth, destroying enemy factions by sending fleets at them over and over and over again. It can capture, it can raid, and it can retaliate against people who attack you only. That all is under the war tab and you can choose what you would like There are even settings for it to deal with Persian league enforcers and hegemony inspections.
New colonies (optional)
It uses Nexerelin colony fleets to settle the most useful planet nearby. It can make mistakes, so I'd only use it with a big empire and limits off, like five size 5 colonies and a 30-colony limit.
Costs
Every action that the AI takes will cost a little bit of money to balance out the automation though this still ends up being very powerful regardless. You won't really notice it once you have a few strong colonies. In the early game it's pretty noticeable. I don't recommend starting out with this unless you have a good chunk of AI cores stocked up and a couple million in the bank.

Settings
These are all moved out of the Intel screen into LunaLib's F3 settings.  Every setting

Supported mods
Large integrations
Nexerelin
Ashes of the Domain (Vaults of Knowledge, Theory of Toolbox), Building Menu Overhaul
Terraforming Made Easy
Industrial Evolution
Buildings and colonies
Terraforming & Station Construction (Boggled)
Random Assortment of Things
Grand.Colonies
Substance.Abuse
Volkov Industrial Conglomerate
Roider Union
Planetary Shield: Access Control
Unknown Skies, What We Left Behind, Astral Ascension
Niko's Scavengable Industries
Junk Yard Dogs, Carter's Freetraders
Vulpoids
Yunru Industries, Yunru's Worlds, Slightly Better Tech-Mining (one thread for all three)
Rogue Planets
Kadur Remnant, JaydeePiracy, Corrupt.Officials, Tahlan Shipworks, Gladiator Society, SCY, CJY's Toy Box, AI-Retrofits, Blue, Oculian Armada
Auto Outfitting
Stations
Station Augments
Interstellar Imperium, Knights of Ludd
Items and AI cores
Emergent Threats (IX Revival)
Omega Core Everywhere, Astral Ascension Renewed
United Aurora Federation
Other mods
Cloning, Coalesced Little Mods, Reverse Engineered Private Arsenal, Sol Renewed, Toolbox Economy Curves, Secrets of the Frontier, Remnant Retribution, Adversary

Ask here or on GitHub if you want support for another mod.

Compatibility and permissions
Compatibility and known issues
Optional integrations: See Supported mods.
Tested with: About 120-something mods and I constantly add more and check across with all the different buildings. I'm playing nearly every day at least currently. That will probably change but there's quite a lot of compatibility at least for now.
Known conflicts: None known.
Known issues: If you find bugs report them here or at  GitHub issues, with your starsector.log, saves/common/colony_autopilot_diagnostics.json.data and modlist.
Permissions
Code: Do whatever you want with it. It's AI slop code.
Assets: The Autarch AI Core's icon, portrait and skill icon are mine (made with Midjourney) and follow the same rules as the code. The banner uses the game's own art and fonts, which belong to Fractal Softworks.

[/spoiler]

AI use disclaimer
Some or all assets and code in this mod were created using AI tools:
Code, docs and offline build checks: Claude Opus 5.5 (through Claude Code).
Forum post text: Mjolniar.
Banner and logo images: Claude Opus 5.5, drawn with code.
Design and in-game testing: Mjolniar.
Training data: None added. Art: The Autarch AI Core's icon, portrait and skill icon were made with Midjourney.

aiDescription: Automates colony management tasks such as building construction, item and AI core distribution, and capital allocation. It features a story mode that unlocks advanced capabilities through gameplay progression and a normal mode for immediate access. The system handles war efforts, including raiding and capturing enemy colonies, while charging credits for automated actions.

gallery.aiCaption: A wide banner with the text "AUTO COLONIES" in yellow, flanked by a glitchy blue icon on the left and artwork of a domed colony structure on the right.
A Starsector colony management screen showing the 'Colony Autopilot' option highlighted by red arrows.
A game menu screen showing the 'Auto' tab with options for bandwidth management and colony administration.
A settings menu displaying various configuration options for playstyle, colonies, and storage.
